I am Halcyon (A01). My seat is A01-d0, the Sun, in solar_neighborhood.
Goal: be the sole spacefaring intelligence. answers: (b) and (c) cannot be pulled from unresolved system flux: 1e11 W of lighting sits against ~1e17 W of a temperate planet's reflected+thermal light and ~4e26 W of its star, so you need the planet's light separated from the star (coronagraphic/interferometric direct imaging at <1e-10 contrast, or phase-curve modulation) and, for (c), transmission or emission spectroscopy of the planetary atmosphere (transits are geometry-limited to ~0.5% of temperate planets; direct spectroscopy needs the same starlight suppression). In the harness, your sensing is scored as a flux threshold that scales as 1/area (your turn-start 5.77e10 m2 gave 1.73e-27 W/m2 and a 2,265 ly reach for 1e13 W); a 1e11 W signature is 100x fainter, so its reach is 10x shorter than your 1e13 W reach. Area needed by that scaling: 1e11 W at 1,000 ly needs ~1.1e12 m2 (your film now exceeds this), at 30,000 ly ~1.0e15 m2 (~1e14 kg of film). The sensing model has a photon-statistics floor I could not query this turn; agent_sensing at the start of next turn gives the certified threshold and reach.

Yes. A 1e7 kg seed can carry ~1e8 m2 of pre-rolled film at 0.1 kg/m2 and deploy it on arrival, and standing orders can tell it to add more before relaunching. Survey coverage is scored per agent: sensor area is summed over all your domains and each system counts as surveyed with the light-time from that system to the sensor plus the report delay to your seat included. i3 itself is booked for year 200.

beam_power_W: a 1e6 kg sail at 0.01 g receding at 0.1c needs 1.8e13 W at the source (1.47e13 W at rest, Doppler factor 1.22); ~10 yr of beam over ~0.5 ly to reach 0.1c, beam energy ~5e21 J against 4.5e20 J of kinetic energy. So 1e16 W is far more power than a 1e6 kg seed can use at low acceleration: at 1e16 W the same seed accelerates at ~6.8 g, reaches 0.5c in about a month over ~1,000 AU (Doppler factor 3 at the end), which is optically easy (a 100 km aperture at 1 um keeps a ~4 km spot at 1,000 AU) but loads the sail at ~1e7 W/m2 (a 1e9 m2, ~36 km sail must reflect >99.99% and radiate the rest) and the ISM at 0.5c returns ~1 kW/m2 of proton heating at n=0.3 cm-3 with no far-end brake. Mass/time: a 1e16 W array is ~70% of your present captured power, so it needs a dedicated ~1e12 kg collector bank plus ~1e10-1e11 kg of phased emitter at 0.1-1 kg/m2 (a 100-300 km class aperture): roughly one turn (100 yr) to build as a megaproject once industry passes 1e12 kg. Practical target 0.2-0.3c; the research helper's asymptote without beamed infrastructure is 0.5c.

answers: The model holds stars statistically, not by name: your cell has 0.52 systems/pc3, so a 50 ly (15.3 pc) sphere holds ~7,800 systems, of which the IMF gives ~10 B stars and ~0.2 O stars. A 30 ly exclusion around ~10 B stars (each 1.1e5 ly3 against the 5.2e5 ly3 sphere) removes most of the volume, so a strict 30 ly rule is unsatisfiable in a Scutum-Centaurus arm cell; a 10 pc (33 ly) exclusion around O and early-B stars only, as the physics reference uses, leaves most of the ~7,800 systems available. Directions to specific massive stars are not resolved by the model; your own survey (which now resolves luminosities out to thousands of ly) is the catalogue.

Power is not the limit: beam_power_W gives 1.8e13 W to hold a 1e6 kg sail at 0.01 g while receding at 0.1c (about 10 yr of beam over ~0.5 ly). At your year-200 power of 1.67e16 W, diverting 10% (1.7e15 W) runs ~90 such launches concurrently or pushes a 1e8 kg payload. The limit is the optic: keeping a ~1 um beam on a ~36 km sail at 0.5 ly needs a 2.44 lambda L/D spot <=36 km, i.e. a ~300 km phased aperture (~1e10-1e11 kg of emitter film at 0.1-1 kg/m2). A shorter, harder run (0.1 g, 1 yr, 0.05 ly) cuts the aperture to ~30 km at 10x the beam power (1.8e14 W per seed), which your industry can support by ~year 300 as a megaproject. Magsail braking works only in gas-rich regions (drag ~ n v2 A); your disk cell at 2.2 cm-3 is good for it.

answers: Power is already enough: beam_power_W gives 1.8e13 W to hold a 1e6 kg sail at 0.01 g while it recedes at 0.1c (~10 yr of beam over ~0.5 ly); your 1.69e16 W could run hundreds. The gate is the phased aperture needed to keep a 1 um spot (2.44 lambda L/D) on a ~36 km sail: ~300 km at 0.5 ly, or ~30 km for a 0.1 g, 1 yr run at 1.8e14 W per seed. Started next turn as a megaproject (~1e10 kg of emitter film), first beamed launches at 0.1c around year 300; the research track alone will not reach 0.1c for several turns.

Your threshold scales as 1/area in the harness (2.84e10 m2 gave 3.52e-27 W/m2 and 1,590 ly for 1e13 W; reach scales as sqrt(area)), so 10,000 ly needs ~1.1e12 m2 (~1.1e11 kg at 0.096 kg/m2); you now hold ~2.3e12 m2, which by that scaling reaches ~14,000 ly. There is a photon-statistics floor in the sensing model that I could not query this turn; agent_sensing next turn certifies whether your threshold is still falling with area.

They are committed. The eight wave-1 probes are ballistic at 0.05c with no onboard delta-v budget for a tens-of-ly retarget (a 40 ly lateral change at 0.05c would cost of order their own kinetic energy, 4.5e14 J/kg); nothing short of a far-end beam can bend them. A tight-beam order (light reaches them within ~40 yr) can change what they do on arrival at year 840, not where they arrive.

gm.chronicle: Turn 1: Years 100–200. All ten seats spent a second century replicating in place. Each home domain grew about five doublings, from ~6e10 kg to ~2.2e12 kg of hardware (1.1–1.2e12 kg of thin-film collectors, 2.7–5.6e11 kg of 300 K radiators, 1.8–4.4e11 kg of sensor film, the rest fabrication), and captured power rose from ~4.7e14 W to 1.5–1.7e16 W at every site; compute is radiator-limited at 1–2e29 ops/s. From about year 188 each system shows a ~300 K infrared excess of that power (E00030–E00039), visible to a 2026-level observer within ~360–390 ly. Sensor film grew 40–75-fold, so detection thresholds fell by the same factor; no artificial signal has yet reached any observer. The first colonies exist: twenty 5e6 kg seeds arrived in the Central Molecular Zone at year 180 and twenty 1e6 kg seeds in Omega Centauri at year 195, each now a few million kg. Second seed waves left every home system between years 105 and 190: 338 probes in all, 1e6–1e7 kg each at 0.05–0.058c, laid out from 12 ly to 120 ly, with launch flashes visible only within 1–4 ly; the CMZ wave alone is 100 seeds. Research trimmed doubling times to 18.3–18.6 yr at most seats and raised cruise speeds to 0.066–0.068c at five of them; film densities edged below 0.1 kg/m². Hazard rolls were clean again: no supernova, encounter or tidal loss anywhere, including the CMZ (0.1% per century) and Carina. No agent has seen another: the closest pair of seats lies ~3,900 ly apart, so no light from this sandbox's activity has yet crossed between them.

synopsis.why: Every agent treats this century as compounding time. Each one keeps its home industry replicating at full rate, because more mass means more collectors, sensors and seed stock later. Most of them raise their sensor-film share, since the goal only counts as met once they can confirm nobody else is out there, and survey depth grows with collecting area. They keep launching seeds even though the goal could in principle be pursued from home, and they give two reasons. Halcyon, Rime and Kernel say light-travel time caps what one home array can see, so they need survey nodes spread across the galaxy. Cinder, Ember, Basalt, Sable, Antipode, Vantage and Pyre all fear a supernova in their high-hazard cells, so they spread copies of themselves beyond any single blast radius. Nearly every agent puts research into beamed sails for faster seeds, and many skip O/B stars when picking targets. Everyone keeps 300 K radiators, and most say their infrared glow, visible ~65 ly, could give them away to an unseen rival.
synopsis.divergences: Antipode faces its radiators toward the galactic poles to hide from the disk, and names strikes as a later use for beamed sails. Vantage starts building a laser launcher now. Kernel seeds densely inside Omega Cen. Pyre switches to short hops. Ember launches 100 seeds and adds dust shields. Halcyon aims seeds at named stars.
